articles.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
articles.summary: The new MacBook Pro has an OLED touchscreen display. The display can achieve 2,000 nits of maximum brightness, and Apple claims it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. The new laptop is lighter than the previous model at just 3 pounds. The top-of-screen camera notch has been replaced by a Dynamic Island, and the Apple logo on the back of the lid glows like in older models.

articles.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, retaking the world's no. 1 spot on updated, harder benchmarks — but access is limited
articles.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon promises improvements in cybersecurity and complex software engineering. It is now available to selected cybersecurity defenders. A broader release will be available after Google improves guardrails on the model based on feedback. Carbon will launch at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 95% discount for cached inputs. Prices will return to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens when the introductory period ends.

articles.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
articles.summary: Apeiron, a Delta-class suborbital spacecraft from Virgin Galactic, is being moved from Virgin Galactic's Spaceship Factory in Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico. After its arrival, aircraft engineers and technicians will complete work on the vehicle's avionics equipment and flight software. Apeiron will still require several ground tests and test flights before it can make a free flight. Virgin Galactic expects Apeiron's first commercial spaceflight to take place early in the second quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Unveiling The Grid: PCBs made in America, twice as fast as Shenzhen
articles.summary: The Grid is a factory-scale robot that can build circuit boards on demand. Every board takes its own route through the factory, which has machines that print solder paste, place parts, reflow, solder, and inspect. With The Grid, printing one unit of 100 designs is as easy as printing 100 units of one, and prototypes and production batches run on the same machines. It allows companies to manufacture huge numbers of low-volume boards, and could help bring manufacturing back to the US.

articles.title: Introducing the Slack Code API: Your agents, your team, one code channel
articles.summary: The Slack Code API allows agents to start code channels, add relevant people and files, post updates as they work, and archive channels when the work is done. It enables teams to work together with agents on tasks with the same shared context. Users can see exactly what agents are doing and who approved it, and workspace controls and data boundaries are built in. Users can choose what agents and models they want to use to suit their needs.

articles.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
articles.summary: Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for a while, but the games weren't fun. The latest generation of models exhibit meaningful improvements in game design, allowing them to create games with novel, compelling gameplay loops. The challenge now is coming up with concepts for games that wouldn't exist without AI assistance.

articles.title: The Sane Asylum
articles.summary: It is now possible to build a highly profitable business with significant scale without raising or hiring a ton. Founders can take advantage of new AI tools to generate financial freedom and build organizations to work on the things they want to, with the people they want, at a scale, ambition, and pace that works for them. This article explores how the founders of turbopuffer, a startup that powers the search infrastructure for many AI companies, built their company. It explores what life and work in the time of AI can look like, and shows how ambitious builders and founders can try it for themselves.

articles.title: Google Shares Fall 10% as Growth in Search Revenue Slows
articles.summary: Google's advertising business failed to deliver on analysts' estimates in the third quarter. The company is still figuring out how to translate AI into faster sales in its core web-search business. While Alphabet reported 25% revenue for the quarter, revenue from search advertising decelerated. Its cloud business exceeded analyst expectations, drawing in $30.7 billion out of Alphabet's total of $127.6 billion in sales.
